A standalone original-adjacency four-cycle checker independently verifies all coefficients through boards of size 4 by 5 and further algebraic cases; finite tests are not substituted for proof.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Rook graph equals the line graph of a complete bipartite graph. Isolating a four-cycle in the line graph differs from deleting four-cycles of the bipartite root graph; the latter has no clique-based non-induced four-cycles within a row. Searches for these equivalent names returned no enumerator. A residual 1-by-3 rook graph and a residual 2-by-2 rook graph have the same maximum degree two but opposite four-cycle status; no uniform star-isolation threshold can encode the predicate.
